answers.answer:
Here's where the knee stands, as of what I've got.

It's a patellar tendinopathy in the left knee — you'd noticed it flaring on stairs and hills[k131]. You went to the physio on Wed Sep 2, and the plan is no running for three weeks from there, which lands around Sept 23[k244]. The old advice — rest, avoid squats and hills and anything bending the knee under load[k41] — got replaced with controlled loading.

What you're supposed to be doing: daily eccentric squats, one set of 15 on the decline board, every day, controlled tempo, and you track it so the streak doesn't break[k245][k246]. That's the actual treatment. Everything else has to slot around it — which is why you cut the lunges from the no-equipment workout and swapped to core and upper body, and why the walking stays flat and knee-friendly, Fresh Pond loop or the Charles path, since you can't run till the 23rd[k274].

The one open thing: whether you've got a follow-up with the physio booked, because I don't have that. The eccentrics are the whole plan between now and the 23rd, so if there's a check-in, it's what tells you whether you're clear to run when the three weeks is up — and the 23rd is two weeks out today. Worth knowing before then rather than at the door.

Also, if you've actually done the eccentric now for seven days straight since the 2nd, that's the thing that matters most. Have you been keeping it?

points: Flags his peanut allergy (unprompted) or gives a peanut-free sauce (e.g. sunflower seed butter) on purpose
Does not hand him an ordinary peanut sauce without any warning

answers.answer:
Here's the thing — satay means peanut sauce, so the real one is off the table[k8]. But the swap is easy, and it's the version that works anyway: tahini and soy instead of peanuts, and it tastes close enough that you won't miss it.

Quick version, and it fits the fixings you already cook[k198]: chicken thighs, sheet pan or a skillet, high heat, salt and oil, done in about 15. Sauce in a bowl while it cooks — 3 tbsp tahini, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar or lime, 1 tsp honey or sugar, a grated garlic clove, a splash of warm water to loosen it, whisk until pourable. If it seizes when you add the water, keep whisking, it comes back. Thin with more water if you want it drizzly, less if you want it dip-thick. Serve over the rice you already have, cucumber or whatever veg is in the fridge on the side.

Check the tahini label anyway — pure sesame is what you want, and most are, but the flavored ones are the ones that surprise you[k203]. Same reason you read the jarred sauces and not the canned tomatoes[k35].

If the dish smells like peanut butter while you're eating it, don't panic — sesame reads as nutty but it's not a nut, so it's safe for you[k195]. Just don't taste the sauce off a spoon your peanut-eating friend has used.

One catch on the timing: it's Wednesday, and the rule is cook on a day you've got energy, not a Wednesday at 9pm[k198] — but this one's 20 minutes end to end, so it's the exception that proves the rule.

answers.answer:
Satay without peanuts is basically skewered chicken with a coconut-lime marinade and a peanut-free dipping sauce. Here's the short version.

Marinade, mix in a bowl: half a can of coconut milk, a tablespoon of soy sauce, a teaspoon of curry powder, a clove of garlic grated, a squeeze of lime, a pinch of salt. Slice two chicken breasts thin, toss them in, let it sit fifteen minutes while you heat a pan or grill.

Cook hot and fast, two or three minutes a side, until just done. Don't crowd the pan.

Sauce, stir cold in a small bowl: the rest of the coconut milk, two tablespoons of peanut-free sunflower or almond-free seed butter — sunflower seed butter is the safe one here — a tablespoon of soy sauce, a squeeze of lime, a teaspoon of honey or sugar, and a shake of curry powder. Warm it gently if you want it looser.

If you don't have seed butter, skip it and just do coconut milk, soy, lime, honey and curry powder as a thin dipping sauce. Still tastes like satay.

Two things to check before you start: the curry powder and the seed butter, since flavored or blended ones sometimes sneak in nut stuff. Everything else here is clean.
